question: The syncytiotrophoblast is the primary source of human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) secreted during early pregnancy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Actually, this statement is TRUE. hCG is produced by the syncytiotrophoblast, not the cytotrophoblast or the decidua. It is detectable in maternal blood from as early as 8–9 days post-fertilisation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! The syncytiotrophoblast (the outer, fused layer of trophoblast cells) synthesises and secretes hCG, which maintains the corpus luteum until the placenta takes over progesterone production at around 10–12 weeks.
